purpose: Machine-readable oracle for automated rule-conformance tests. The game follows the selected project variant, not every variant described by each source.

severityPolicy.bug: Implementation contradicts an enforced project rule.
severityPolicy.source_divergence: Project intentionally chose one variant although another supplied source describes a different variant. Report, do not fail.
severityPolicy.review: The supplied sources and explicit project decisions do not uniquely determine the behavior. Report for human review; never auto-fix.

rules.projectRule: Use one standard 52-card deck, without jokers, for 1 human plus 2 or 3 bots.
rules.basis: Both sources describe a standard 52-card deck as sufficient for 2-4 players; jokers are optional. Project explicitly selected no jokers and max 3 bots.

rules.projectRule: Deal 5 cards to every player; the initial face-up card must be non-functional.
A normal play must match the top card by suit or rank unless an explicitly selected functional-card rule overrides it.
A turn may play exactly 1, 3 or 4 cards of the same rank. Pairs and stair/runs are disabled.
rules.basis: Project selected the Morele 1/3/4 variant. Wikipedia describes broader multi-card variants.

rules.projectRule: When a normally drawn card is immediately legal, it may be played in the same turn ('pierwsza karta ratuje'). Only that newly drawn card is playable as the rescue play.
rules.basis: Project explicitly selected the Wikipedia rescue rule. Morele describes drawing and losing the turn. Restricting the rescue play to the newly drawn card is the current project interpretation.

rules.projectRule: 2 adds 2 cards and 3 adds 3 cards to the pending penalty. Defense is only another 2 or 3 that also matches the current top card by suit or rank. Multiple 2s/3s played together add the total pip value.
rules.basis: Both sources describe 2/3 penalties and accumulation; project explicitly clarified suit-or-rank matching and total pip summation.

rules.projectRule: 4 blocks the next player for one turn; additional 4s accumulate blocked turns. The direct defense to an active block is another 4.
Current implementation resolves a pending 2/3 draw penalty even if the target also has an older blocked turn, consuming the block and the penalty together.
rules.basis: Wikipedia additionally says functional effects do not act on a blocked player and are applied to the next player; this interaction was not explicitly selected when the project variant was established.

rules.projectRule: Jack may demand a non-functional numeric rank 5-10 that the actor still holds after playing the Jack, or demand nothing. A Jack can answer an existing Jack demand. Bots should not create endless Jack-demand loops.
rules.basis: Sources support Jack demands for non-functional values and Wikipedia explicitly allows changing a Jack demand to no demand. Requiring the demanded rank to be held is an explicit project clarification from the user.

rules.projectRule: Queen is wild in normal play ('dama na wszystko, wszystko na dame') but may not bypass an active draw penalty, block, Jack demand or Ace demand.
rules.basis: Project explicitly selected the restricted-queen variant mentioned by Wikipedia; Morele only describes the common broad queen rule.

rules.projectRule: Ace demands a suit for the next player only. That player may answer with the demanded suit or another Ace.
rules.basis: Supported by Wikipedia; Morele describes Ace as a suit-demand card in general terms.

rules.projectRule: K-hearts immediately makes the next active player draw 5. K-spades immediately makes the previous active player draw 5. K-clubs and K-diamonds are ordinary cards. No king counter/defense chain is used.
rules.basis: Direction and +5 are supported by both sources. Project explicitly disabled all special behavior for K-clubs/K-diamonds; Wikipedia describes king counter/block variants that are intentionally not used.

rules.projectRule: A human reaching one card must declare MAKAO. Missing the declaration allows STOP MAKAO and causes +5 cards. Finishing all cards uses the project's 'Makao i po makale' declaration flow.
rules.basis: Both sources support the one-card declaration and +5 penalty; Morele also describes 'makao i po makale' when finishing in one play.

rules.projectRule: When the draw pile is empty, shuffle the discard pile back into a new draw pile while preserving the current top discard card.
After the first player finishes, remaining players continue until the complete placement order is known.
rules.basis: Project explicitly selected the Wikipedia continuation rule. Morele describes the game as ending when the first player has no cards.
